title: Clean Hands Save Lives
paras: Germs are everywhere in a hospital. They are on bed rails, door handles, and phones. Many germs are too small to see, but they can make patients very sick.

The easiest way to stop germs is to clean your hands. Nurses clean their hands before they touch a patient and after they touch a patient. They also clean their hands after they take off their gloves.
You can use hand gel or soap and water. Rub the gel on all parts of your hands until they are dry. If your hands look dirty, wash them with soap and water for at least twenty seconds.
Visitors should clean their hands too. It only takes a few seconds, and it can save a life.
zh: 醫院到處都有細菌，在床欄、門把和電話上，很多小到看不見，卻能讓病人生重病。阻止細菌最簡單的方法是清潔雙手：護理師碰病人前後都要，脫手套後也要。可以用乾洗手或肥皂和水：乾洗手要搓到手的每個地方直到乾；手看起來髒時，用肥皂和水洗至少 20 秒。訪客也要清潔雙手，只要幾秒鐘就可能救一條命。

qs.q: What is the main idea of the text?
options: Gloves are better than hand gel
Cleaning your hands stops germs in hospitals
qs.why: 整篇都在講清潔雙手可以阻止醫院裡的細菌。

qs.q: When should you wash your hands with soap and water?
qs.why: If your hands look dirty, wash them with soap and water：手看起來髒就用肥皂和水洗。
qs.evidence: If your hands look dirty, wash them with soap and water for at least twenty seconds.

qs.q: Nurses clean their hands after they take off their gloves.
qs.why: 文章說脫手套後也要清潔雙手。
qs.evidence: They also clean their hands after they take off their gloves.

qs.q: "Rub the gel on all parts of your hands." Here "rub" means…
options: move your hands against each other
qs.why: rub 是來回搓揉，把乾洗手搓到整隻手。
qs.evidence: Rub the gel on all parts of your hands until they are dry.

title: Help Us Keep You Safe From Falls
paras: Many patients fall in the hospital. Falls can cause broken bones and head injuries, so we want to keep you safe.
Some medicines can make you dizzy or sleepy. Being in bed for many days can also make your legs weak.

Please follow these tips. Use the call button before you get out of bed, especially at night. Wear the non-slip socks we give you. Keep your glasses and your phone close to your bed. Sit on the edge of the bed for a minute before you stand up.
If you feel dizzy, sit down right away and call us. We are happy to help you every time.
zh: 很多病人會在醫院跌倒，可能骨折或頭部受傷。有些藥會讓人頭暈或想睡，臥床很多天腿也會變無力。請照做：下床前先按呼叫鈴，尤其是晚上；穿我們給的防滑襪；眼鏡和手機放在床邊；站起來前先在床邊坐一分鐘。覺得頭暈就馬上坐下並叫我們，每次我們都很樂意幫忙。

qs.q: Who is this text for?
qs.why: 文中一直用 you 對病人說話，教病人怎麼防跌。

qs.q: Why can patients' legs become weak?
options: They stay in bed for many days
qs.why: 臥床很多天會讓腿變無力。
qs.evidence: Being in bed for many days can also make your legs weak.

qs.q: What should you do before you stand up?
options: Sit on the edge of the bed for a minute
qs.why: 站起來之前先在床邊坐一分鐘。
qs.evidence: Sit on the edge of the bed for a minute before you stand up.

qs.q: Falls in the hospital never cause serious injuries.
qs.why: 文章說跌倒會造成骨折和頭部受傷，和題目相反。
qs.evidence: Falls can cause broken bones and head injuries

title: Visiting Information
paras: Welcome to Ward 7B. We know that visits from family and friends help patients feel better.
Visiting hours are from 10 a.m. to 8 p.m. Only two visitors can be with a patient at one time. Children under twelve must come with an adult.
From 2 p.m. to 4 p.m. is quiet time. Patients need to rest, so please keep your voice low and turn off the TV.
Please do not visit if you have a cold, a cough, or a fever. Clean your hands with the gel at the door when you come in and when you leave. Flowers are not allowed in the intensive care unit.
If you have any questions, please ask at the nurses' station.
zh: 歡迎來到 7B 病房，家人朋友來探望能讓病人感覺好一點。探病時間是早上 10 點到晚上 8 點，每次只能兩位訪客，12 歲以下兒童要有大人陪。下午 2 點到 4 點是安靜時間，病人要休息，請小聲並關掉電視。感冒、咳嗽或發燒請不要來；進出時用門口的乾洗手清潔雙手。加護病房不能帶花。有問題請到護理站問。

qs.q: How many visitors can be with a patient at one time?
qs.why: 一次只能兩位訪客。
qs.evidence: Only two visitors can be with a patient at one time.

qs.q: What happens from 2 p.m. to 4 p.m.?
qs.why: 下午 2 點到 4 點是安靜時間。
qs.evidence: From 2 p.m. to 4 p.m. is quiet time.

qs.q: Children under twelve cannot visit.
qs.why: 可以來，只是要有大人陪，所以「不能來」是錯的。
qs.evidence: Children under twelve must come with an adult.

qs.q: Visitors can park for free.
qs.why: 文章完全沒有提到停車。

title: Tell Us About Your Pain
paras: Pain is not something you have to live with in the hospital. Your nurse will ask about your pain many times a day.
We use a scale from 0 to 10. 0 means no pain, and 10 means the worst pain you can imagine. You can also point to faces on a chart, from a happy face to a crying face.
Tell us where it hurts and what it feels like. Is it sharp, dull, burning, or throbbing? Does it come and go, or is it there all the time?

Please tell us early. Pain is easier to control when it is not too strong. Medicine is not the only way to help. Ice packs, warm packs, music, and changing your position can also make you feel better.
zh: 住院時疼痛不是只能忍，護理師一天會問你好幾次。我們用 0 到 10 分：0 是不痛，10 是能想像最痛的；也可以指表上從笑臉到哭臉的臉。告訴我們哪裡痛、是什麼感覺：刺痛、悶痛、燒灼痛還是抽痛？一陣一陣還是一直痛？請早點說，疼痛不太強的時候比較好控制。除了藥，冰敷、熱敷、音樂和換姿勢也能讓你舒服一點。

qs.q: What is the main message of the text?
options: Tell the nurse about your pain early
Pain is normal, so don't talk about it
qs.why: 文章重點是請病人早點、清楚地說出疼痛。

qs.q: What does 10 mean on the scale?
options: The worst pain you can imagine
qs.why: 10 是你能想像最痛的。
qs.evidence: 10 means the worst pain you can imagine.

qs.q: Why should you tell the nurse early?
options: Medicine is cheaper in the morning
Pain is easier to control when it is not too strong
qs.why: 疼痛不太強時比較好控制。
qs.evidence: Pain is easier to control when it is not too strong.

qs.q: Music can help some patients feel better.
qs.why: 文章把音樂列在讓人舒服一點的方法裡。
qs.evidence: Ice packs, warm packs, music, and changing your position can also make you feel better.

title: Your Fasting Blood Test
paras: Your doctor ordered a fasting blood test for tomorrow morning. This test checks your blood sugar and your cholesterol.
Fasting means no food. Please do not eat anything after 8 p.m. tonight. You can drink water, and water is good for you. Please do not drink coffee, tea, juice, or milk.
Ask your nurse about your morning medicines. Some medicines are OK to take with a little water, but some should wait until after the test.
The test is at 7 a.m. It takes about five minutes. After the test, you can eat breakfast right away.
zh: 醫師開了明天早上的空腹抽血，檢查血糖和膽固醇。空腹就是不能吃東西：今晚 8 點後什麼都不要吃。可以喝水，但不要喝咖啡、茶、果汁或牛奶。早上的藥要先問護理師，有些可以配一點水吃，有些要等抽完血。抽血在早上 7 點，大約 5 分鐘，抽完就可以馬上吃早餐。

qs.q: "Fasting means no food." Which is the best meaning of "fasting"?
qs.why: fasting 是一段時間不吃東西（空腹、禁食）。
qs.evidence: Fasting means no food.

qs.q: What can the patient drink before the test?
qs.why: 只可以喝水，咖啡、茶、果汁、牛奶都不行。
qs.evidence: You can drink water, and water is good for you.

qs.q: When can the patient eat?
qs.why: 抽完血就可以馬上吃早餐。
qs.evidence: After the test, you can eat breakfast right away.

qs.q: The patient should not take any medicine in the morning.
qs.why: 文章說有些藥可以配一點水吃，要先問護理師，所以「什麼藥都不能吃」是錯的。
qs.evidence: Some medicines are OK to take with a little water

title: My First Night Shift
paras: Last Friday, I worked my first night shift as a nursing student. It started at eleven at night and finished at seven in the morning.

At night, the ward was very quiet. Most patients were asleep, but the nurses were busy. Every two hours, we checked each patient. We looked at their breathing and their IV lines, and we turned patients who could not move.
At three o'clock, an old man woke up and felt confused. He wanted to go home. My preceptor spoke to him softly and turned on a small light. After a few minutes, he felt calm and went back to sleep.
In the morning, I was very tired, but I learned that a calm voice can be strong medicine.
zh: 上週五我以護生身分上了第一個大夜班，晚上 11 點到早上 7 點。晚上病房很安靜，大部分病人在睡，但護理師很忙：每兩小時巡一次病人，看呼吸和點滴，幫不能動的病人翻身。三點時一位老先生醒來意識混亂想回家，我的指導護理師輕聲跟他說話、開一盞小燈，幾分鐘後他平靜下來又睡著了。早上我很累，但學到冷靜的聲音也可以是一帖良藥。

qs.q: How long was the night shift?
qs.why: 晚上 11 點到早上 7 點，總共 8 小時。
qs.evidence: It started at eleven at night and finished at seven in the morning.

qs.q: How often did they check each patient?
qs.why: 每兩小時巡一次。
qs.evidence: Every two hours, we checked each patient.

qs.q: "He wanted to go home." Who is "he"?
qs.why: 前一句說一位老先生醒來，he 就是他。
qs.evidence: an old man woke up and felt confused

qs.q: What did the writer learn?
options: A calm voice can help patients
Old patients should not stay in hospital
qs.why: 最後一句：冷靜的聲音可以是一帖良藥。
qs.evidence: a calm voice can be strong medicine

title: Two Ways to Check Who You Are
paras: In our hospital, every patient wears a wristband. It shows your name and your date of birth.

Before we give you medicine, take your blood, or take you for a test, we will ask you two questions: "What is your name?" and "What is your date of birth?" Then we check your answers against your wristband.
Some patients ask, "Why do you ask me again? You already know me!" We ask every time because many patients have the same or similar names. A small mistake can be very dangerous.
Please help us. Say your full name and your date of birth every time we ask. If your wristband comes off or has the wrong information, tell a nurse right away.
zh: 本院每位病人都戴手圈，上面有姓名和出生日期。給藥、抽血或帶你去檢查前，我們會問你叫什麼名字、出生日期是什麼，再跟手圈核對。有些病人會問：你們不是已經認識我了嗎？我們每次都問，因為很多病人名字一樣或很像，小錯可能很危險。請每次都說出全名和生日；手圈掉了或資料不對，要馬上告訴護理師。

qs.q: What two things are on the wristband?
options: The doctor's name and phone number
qs.why: 手圈上有姓名和出生日期。
qs.evidence: It shows your name and your date of birth.

qs.q: Why do nurses ask every time?
options: It is a new rule this year
Many patients have the same or similar names
qs.why: 很多病人名字一樣或很像。
qs.evidence: many patients have the same or similar names

qs.q: Patients should tell a nurse if their wristband comes off.
qs.why: 手圈掉了要馬上告訴護理師。
qs.evidence: If your wristband comes off or has the wrong information, tell a nurse right away.

title: Sleeping Well in the Hospital
paras: It can be hard to sleep in the hospital. Machines beep, lights are on, and nurses come in at night.
Nurses need to check you at night, but you can still get good rest. Here are some ideas.

Ask for earplugs or an eye mask. Try not to sleep a lot during the day. Turn off your phone an hour before bed. If pain keeps you awake, tell your nurse. A warm drink without caffeine, like milk, may help you relax.
If you still cannot sleep for many nights, talk to your doctor. Good sleep helps your body heal.
zh: 在醫院可能很難睡：機器嗶嗶響、燈開著、護理師半夜會進來。護理師晚上要巡你，但你還是可以好好休息：要耳塞或眼罩、白天別睡太多、睡前一小時關手機；痛到睡不著要告訴護理師；一杯不含咖啡因的熱飲，像牛奶，可能幫你放鬆。連續很多晚都睡不著就跟醫師說。睡得好能幫助身體復原。

qs.q: What is the text about?
options: Ideas to help patients sleep in the hospital
qs.why: 整篇在給住院睡不好的人建議。

qs.q: When should you turn off your phone?
qs.why: 睡前一小時關手機。
qs.evidence: Turn off your phone an hour before bed.

qs.q: Patients can ask for earplugs.
qs.why: 文章建議可以要耳塞或眼罩。
qs.evidence: Ask for earplugs or an eye mask.

title: Contact Precautions: Information for Visitors
paras: The patient in this room has an infection that can spread by touch. The germs can live on skin, on clothes, and on things in the room, such as the bed rails, the TV remote, and the bathroom door.

To protect yourself and other patients, please follow these steps. Clean your hands before you go in. Put on a gown and gloves before you touch the patient or anything in the room. You do not need a mask unless a nurse tells you to wear one.

Before you leave, take off your gloves and gown inside the room and throw them in the bin by the door. Then clean your hands again. Please do not sit on the patient's bed, and do not use the patient's bathroom.

These rules can feel strange, especially for close family. However, they are the best way to stop the infection from spreading to other people in the hospital and to your family at home. If you have any questions, please ask the nurse caring for the patient.
zh: 這間病人的感染會經由接觸傳播，細菌可以留在皮膚、衣服和房間物品上，例如床欄、遙控器和浴室門。為保護你和其他病人：進房前清潔雙手；碰病人或房內任何東西前穿隔離衣、戴手套；除非護理師要求，不需要戴口罩。離開前在房內脫掉手套和隔離衣，丟進門邊的桶子，再清潔雙手。不要坐病人的床，也不要用病人的廁所。這些規定對家人來說可能很奇怪，但這是阻止感染傳給醫院其他人和家裡的人最好的方法。有問題請問照顧病人的護理師。

qs.q: What is the purpose of this text?
options: To explain how visitors can stop an infection from spreading
To tell visitors when they can come
To describe the patient's illness in detail
qs.why: 整篇都在教訪客怎麼做才不會讓感染傳出去。

qs.q: Where should visitors take off their gown?
qs.why: 要在病房裡面脫掉手套和隔離衣。
qs.evidence: take off your gloves and gown inside the room

qs.q: Visitors must always wear a mask in this room.
qs.why: 文章說除非護理師要求，不需要戴口罩。
qs.evidence: You do not need a mask unless a nurse tells you to wear one.

qs.q: The patient will stay in isolation for two weeks.
qs.why: 文章沒說要隔離多久。

title: Living With Heart Failure
paras: Heart failure does not mean that your heart has stopped. It means that your heart is not pumping as well as it should. Because of this, fluid can build up in your body, especially in your legs and lungs.

The most important thing you can do at home is to weigh yourself every morning. Do it at the same time, after you use the toilet and before you eat breakfast. Write the number in a notebook. A quick weight gain is often the first sign that fluid is building up.

Call your doctor if you gain more than two pounds in one day or five pounds in one week. Also call if your ankles swell, if you need more pillows to breathe at night, or if you feel more tired than usual.

Eat less salt, because salt makes your body hold on to water. Read food labels, and avoid fast food, instant noodles, and canned soup. Take your medicines every day, even when you feel well. If you have chest pain or serious trouble breathing, call 911 right away.
zh: 心臟衰竭不是心臟停了，而是心臟打血不如應有的好，所以水分會積在身體裡，尤其是腿和肺。在家最重要的是每天早上量體重：同一時間、上完廁所、吃早餐前，記在本子上，體重突然增加常是積水的第一個徵兆。一天重了超過 2 磅或一週超過 5 磅要打給醫師；腳踝腫、晚上要墊更多枕頭才能呼吸，或比平常更累也要打。少吃鹽，因為鹽會讓身體留住水；看食品標示，避開速食、泡麵和罐頭湯。每天吃藥，覺得好也要吃。胸痛或嚴重呼吸困難要馬上打 911。

qs.q: What is the main idea of the text?
options: Why heart failure means the heart has stopped
How to cook food without salt
How people with heart failure can take care of themselves at home
qs.why: 文章教心衰竭病人在家怎麼照顧自己：量體重、少鹽、吃藥、什麼時候求助。

qs.q: When should the patient weigh themselves?
options: Every morning after using the toilet, before breakfast
Once a week at the doctor's office
qs.why: 每天早上、上完廁所、吃早餐前。
qs.evidence: Do it at the same time, after you use the toilet and before you eat breakfast.

qs.q: "Fluid can build up in your body." Here "build up" means…
qs.why: build up 是慢慢累積、越積越多。
qs.evidence: fluid can build up in your body

qs.q: Which sentence explains why patients should eat less salt?
options: "Salt makes your body hold on to water."
qs.why: because 後面就是原因：鹽會讓身體留住水。
qs.evidence: salt makes your body hold on to water

title: Low Blood Sugar: What to Do
paras: People who take insulin or some diabetes pills can get low blood sugar, which is also called hypoglycemia. This usually means a blood sugar level below 70.
Common signs are shaking, sweating, a fast heartbeat, hunger, and feeling dizzy or confused. Some people become angry or act strangely, so family members may notice it first.

If you think your sugar is low, check it right away. If it is below 70, follow the "rule of 15": eat or drink 15 grams of fast sugar, such as half a cup of fruit juice or regular soda, or three or four glucose tablets. Wait 15 minutes, then check again. If it is still below 70, repeat these steps.

When your sugar is back to normal, eat a small snack with protein if your next meal is more than an hour away. If you are confused or cannot swallow safely, someone should call for help instead of giving you food or drink.
zh: 用胰島素或某些糖尿病藥的人可能低血糖，通常指血糖低於 70。常見徵象有發抖、冒汗、心跳快、餓、頭暈或意識混亂；有些人會生氣或行為怪異，家人可能先發現。覺得血糖低就馬上測，低於 70 用「15 法則」：吃或喝 15 克快速吸收的糖，例如半杯果汁或一般汽水，或 3 到 4 顆葡萄糖片；等 15 分鐘再測，還低於 70 就重複。恢復正常後，如果下一餐還要超過一小時，吃一點有蛋白質的點心。如果意識混亂或無法安全吞嚥，旁人應該叫救援，而不是餵他吃喝。

qs.q: Which is a sign of low blood sugar?
qs.why: 常見徵象：發抖、冒汗、心跳快、餓、頭暈或混亂。
qs.evidence: Common signs are shaking, sweating, a fast heartbeat, hunger, and feeling dizzy or confused.

qs.q: In the "rule of 15", how long should you wait before checking again?
qs.why: 等 15 分鐘再測。
qs.evidence: Wait 15 minutes, then check again.

qs.q: Family members may notice low blood sugar before the patient does.
qs.why: 有些人會生氣或怪怪的，家人可能先發現。
qs.evidence: so family members may notice it first

qs.q: What should happen if the person cannot swallow safely?
qs.why: 不能安全吞嚥時不要餵，應該叫救援。
qs.evidence: someone should call for help instead of giving you food or drink

title: What Is a Pressure Injury?
paras: A pressure injury, also called a bed sore or a pressure ulcer, is damage to the skin and the tissue under it. It happens when something presses on the same area for a long time and blood cannot flow there well.

Pressure injuries often form over bones, such as the tailbone, the hips, the heels, and the back of the head. Patients who cannot move by themselves, are very thin, or have wet skin are at higher risk.

The first sign is often a red area that does not turn white when you press it gently. Later, the skin may break and become an open wound. Deep pressure injuries can take months to heal and can cause serious infections.

Nurses help prevent pressure injuries by turning patients at least every two hours, using special mattresses, keeping the skin clean and dry, and making sure patients get enough protein and fluids. The good news is that most pressure injuries can be prevented.
zh: 壓力性損傷又叫褥瘡或壓瘡，是皮膚和底下組織受損，發生在同一處被壓太久、血液流不過去的時候。常出現在骨頭突出的地方：尾骨、髖部、腳跟和後腦勺；自己不能動、很瘦或皮膚潮濕的病人風險較高。第一個徵象常是一塊發紅、輕壓也不會變白的皮膚，之後可能破掉變成開放性傷口；深的要好幾個月才好，還可能造成嚴重感染。護理師會至少每兩小時翻身、用特殊床墊、保持皮膚清潔乾燥、確保病人有足夠蛋白質和水分。好消息是大部分都可以預防。

qs.q: Where do pressure injuries often form?
options: Over bones, such as the heels and the hips
qs.why: 常出現在骨頭突出的地方，例如尾骨、髖部、腳跟。
qs.evidence: Pressure injuries often form over bones, such as the tailbone, the hips, the heels, and the back of the head.

qs.q: What is often the first sign?
options: A red area that does not turn white when pressed
qs.why: 第一個徵象：發紅、輕壓也不會變白。
qs.evidence: The first sign is often a red area that does not turn white when you press it gently.

qs.q: Patients with wet skin have a higher risk.
qs.why: 皮膚潮濕的病人風險較高。
qs.evidence: or have wet skin are at higher risk

qs.q: Most pressure injuries cannot be prevented.
qs.why: 文章說大部分都可以預防，和題目相反。
qs.evidence: most pressure injuries can be prevented

title: SBAR: A Clear Way to Report
paras: When a patient's condition changes, a nurse often has to call a doctor quickly. If the report is long and confusing, important information can be lost. SBAR is a simple way to organize what you say.

S stands for Situation: who you are, which patient you are calling about, and what the problem is right now. B stands for Background: why the patient is in the hospital and any important history. A stands for Assessment: the vital signs and what you think is happening. R stands for Recommendation: what you want the doctor to do, for example, to come and see the patient or to order a test.

Here is a short example. "This is Nurse Lin on 6 West. Mr. Wang in Room 5 has a new fever of 39 degrees. He had bowel surgery two days ago. His heart rate is 115, and his blood pressure is lower than this morning. I am worried about an infection. Could you come and see him?"
Before the call, have the patient's chart, vital signs, and medicine list ready. After the doctor gives an order, read it back to make sure you heard it correctly.
zh: 病人狀況改變時，護理師常要很快打給醫師；報告又長又亂，重要資訊就可能漏掉。SBAR 是整理說話內容的簡單方法：S（狀況）你是誰、哪位病人、現在的問題；B（背景）為什麼住院和重要病史；A（評估）生命徵象和你認為發生什麼事；R（建議）你希望醫師做什麼，例如來看病人或開檢查。例子：6 西林護理師，5 房王先生新發燒 39 度，兩天前做腸道手術，心跳 115，血壓比早上低，擔心感染，可以請你來看他嗎？打電話前準備好病歷、生命徵象和用藥清單；醫師給醫囑後要複誦確認。

qs.q: What does the B in SBAR stand for?
qs.why: B 是 Background，背景。
qs.evidence: B stands for Background

qs.q: In the example, what is the nurse worried about?
qs.why: I am worried about an infection.
qs.evidence: I am worried about an infection.

qs.q: "Read it back" in the last paragraph means…
options: repeat the order to check it
qs.why: read back 是把醫囑複誦一次，確認聽對。
qs.evidence: read it back to make sure you heard it correctly

qs.q: The nurse should prepare the patient's chart before the call.
qs.why: 打電話前要準備好病歷、生命徵象和用藥清單。
qs.evidence: Before the call, have the patient's chart, vital signs, and medicine list ready.

title: Sudden Confusion in Older Patients
paras: Older patients in the hospital sometimes become confused very suddenly. They may not know where they are, see things that are not there, or be very sleepy during the day and awake at night. This is often delirium.

Delirium is different from dementia. Dementia develops slowly over months or years. Delirium starts over hours or days, and it often gets better and worse during the same day. It is common after surgery and in patients with infections, dehydration, or many new medicines.
Delirium is a medical problem, not just "old age", so nurses should report it to the doctor quickly. The cause must be found and treated.

Simple things can help. Make sure the patient has their glasses and hearing aids. Keep a clock and a calendar in the room. Turn the lights on during the day, and keep the room dark and quiet at night. Family visits and familiar objects, like photos, can also help the patient feel safe.
zh: 住院的長者有時會突然意識混亂：不知道自己在哪、看到不存在的東西，或白天很想睡、晚上醒著，這常是譫妄。譫妄和失智不同：失智是幾個月到幾年慢慢變化；譫妄在幾小時到幾天內出現，同一天內也常好好壞壞，常見於手術後，以及感染、脫水或用了很多新藥的病人。譫妄是醫療問題，不只是老了，護理師要盡快通報醫師，找出原因並治療。簡單的方法有幫助：戴好眼鏡和助聽器、房裡放時鐘和月曆、白天開燈、晚上保持暗和安靜；家人探訪和熟悉的東西如照片也能讓病人安心。

qs.q: What is the main idea of the text?
options: Older patients should not have visitors
Delirium is sudden confusion that needs attention and can be helped
qs.why: 文章說明譫妄是什麼、要通報、以及怎麼幫忙。

qs.q: How is delirium different from dementia?
options: Delirium starts suddenly, over hours or days
qs.why: 譫妄在幾小時到幾天內出現；失智是幾個月到幾年。
qs.evidence: Delirium starts over hours or days

qs.q: Delirium is just a normal part of getting old.
qs.why: 文章說譫妄是醫療問題，不只是老了。
qs.evidence: Delirium is a medical problem, not just "old age"

qs.q: Which can help a patient with delirium?
options: Having a clock and a calendar in the room
Keeping the room bright all night
qs.why: 房裡放時鐘和月曆可以幫助病人。
qs.evidence: Keep a clock and a calendar in the room.

title: Your IV Line
paras: An IV is a thin plastic tube that a nurse puts into a vein, usually in your hand or arm. Through it, we can give you fluids, medicines, and sometimes blood.

Most IVs are comfortable, but please tell your nurse right away if you notice pain, swelling, redness, or a cool or wet feeling around the IV site. These can be signs that the IV is not in the vein anymore or that the area is getting irritated.

Be careful when you move. Do not pull on the tubing, and keep the IV bag above the level of your heart when you walk. If the pump beeps, do not try to fix it yourself. Press the call button and a nurse will come.
Your nurse will check the IV site often and change it when needed. When you no longer need fluids or IV medicines, the IV will be taken out. This only takes a few seconds.
zh: 點滴是護理師放進靜脈的細塑膠管，通常在手或手臂，可以透過它給水分、藥物，有時給血。大部分點滴不會不舒服，但如果注射部位疼痛、腫、紅，或摸起來涼涼濕濕的，要馬上告訴護理師，這可能表示管子不在血管裡了或部位受到刺激。移動時要小心：不要拉管子，走路時點滴袋要高於心臟。點滴機響了不要自己弄，按呼叫鈴護理師會來。護理師會常檢查並在需要時更換；不再需要點滴就會拔掉，只要幾秒鐘。

qs.q: What should you do if the pump beeps?
qs.why: 不要自己弄，按呼叫鈴。
qs.evidence: If the pump beeps, do not try to fix it yourself. Press the call button and a nurse will come.

qs.q: A cool or wet feeling around the IV site can be a warning sign.
qs.why: 涼涼濕濕的感覺是要馬上告訴護理師的徵象之一。
qs.evidence: a cool or wet feeling around the IV site

qs.q: "the area is getting irritated" — here "irritated" means…
qs.why: irritated 是受到刺激、發紅疼痛。
qs.evidence: the area is getting irritated

qs.q: Taking out an IV takes about an hour.
qs.why: 拔點滴只要幾秒鐘。
qs.evidence: This only takes a few seconds.

title: Caring for Your Surgical Wound at Home
paras: Your wound needs a little care while it heals. Most surgical wounds heal well in about two weeks, but this can take longer if you smoke or have diabetes.

Keep the dressing clean and dry. Your surgeon will tell you when you can shower. When you are allowed to shower, let the water run over the wound gently and pat it dry with a clean towel. Do not soak in a bath or go swimming until your doctor says the wound has healed.
Always wash your hands before you touch the wound or change the dressing. Do not put creams or powders on the wound unless your doctor tells you to.

Some pain and a little clear fluid are normal for the first few days. Call your doctor if you notice more redness, swelling, warmth, pus, or a bad smell, or if you have a fever over 38 degrees. If your stitches need to be removed, make an appointment for about ten days after surgery, or when your doctor tells you to.
zh: 傷口在癒合時需要一點照顧。大部分手術傷口約兩週會好，但抽菸或有糖尿病可能更久。保持敷料乾淨乾燥，什麼時候可以淋浴由外科醫師決定；可以淋浴時讓水輕輕流過傷口，用乾淨毛巾輕拍擦乾。醫師說癒合前不要泡澡或游泳。碰傷口或換藥前一定要洗手；除非醫師交代，不要塗乳霜或撒粉。頭幾天有些疼痛和少量清澈液體是正常的；更紅、腫、熱、有膿、有臭味，或發燒超過 38 度要打給醫師。需要拆線的話，約手術後十天，或照醫師說的時間預約。

qs.q: Who decides when you can shower?
qs.why: 外科醫師會告訴你什麼時候可以淋浴。
qs.evidence: Your surgeon will tell you when you can shower.

qs.q: A little clear fluid from the wound is normal in the first few days.
qs.why: 頭幾天有些疼痛和少量清澈液體是正常的。
qs.evidence: Some pain and a little clear fluid are normal for the first few days.

qs.q: Which can make healing slower?
qs.why: 抽菸或糖尿病會讓癒合更久。
qs.evidence: this can take longer if you smoke or have diabetes

qs.q: You should put antibiotic cream on the wound every day.
qs.why: 除非醫師交代，不要在傷口上塗東西。
qs.evidence: Do not put creams or powders on the wound unless your doctor tells you to.

title: The Rights of Medication Safety
paras: Giving medicine is one of a nurse's most important jobs, and mistakes can hurt patients. To prevent errors, nursing students learn the "rights" of medication safety.

The first five are the right patient, the right drug, the right dose, the right route, and the right time. The right patient means checking two identifiers, such as the name and the date of birth. The right route means giving the medicine the correct way, for example by mouth, by injection, or through an IV.

Many hospitals add more rights, such as the right documentation and the patient's right to refuse. After giving a medicine, the nurse must record it. If a patient refuses a medicine, the nurse should find out why, explain the possible risks, and tell the doctor.
Checking the rights only takes a minute, but it protects patients and nurses. If something does not look right, the safest thing to do is to stop and ask.
zh: 給藥是護理師最重要的工作之一，出錯會傷害病人。為了預防錯誤，護生要學給藥安全的「正確」原則。前五個是：正確病人、正確藥物、正確劑量、正確途徑、正確時間。正確病人指核對兩個身分辨識，例如姓名和出生日期；正確途徑指用對的方式給藥，例如口服、注射或靜脈。很多醫院再加上正確記錄和病人拒絕的權利：給藥後要記錄；病人拒絕時要了解原因、說明可能風險並通知醫師。核對只要一分鐘，卻能保護病人和護理師；覺得哪裡不對，最安全的做法是先停下來問。

qs.q: Which is an example of a "route"?
qs.why: 途徑是給藥的方式：口服、注射、靜脈。
qs.evidence: for example by mouth, by injection, or through an IV

qs.q: What should a nurse do if a patient refuses a medicine?
options: Find out why and tell the doctor
Hide it in the patient's food
Give it the next day without asking
qs.why: 要了解原因、說明風險並通知醫師。
qs.evidence: the nurse should find out why, explain the possible risks, and tell the doctor

qs.q: What is the main message of the last paragraph?
options: Stop and ask if something does not look right
qs.why: 最後一段：覺得不對就停下來問。
qs.evidence: the safest thing to do is to stop and ask

qs.q: "two identifiers" means…
options: two pieces of information that show who the patient is
qs.why: identifier 是用來辨認身分的資料，例如姓名和生日。
qs.evidence: checking two identifiers, such as the name and the date of birth

title: Know the Signs of a Stroke: BE FAST
paras: A stroke happens when blood cannot reach part of the brain, or when a blood vessel in the brain breaks. Brain cells start to die within minutes, so fast treatment is very important.

The letters BE FAST can help you remember the warning signs. B is for Balance: sudden dizziness or trouble walking. E is for Eyes: sudden trouble seeing in one or both eyes. F is for Face: one side of the face droops when the person smiles. A is for Arm: one arm drifts down when the person raises both arms. S is for Speech: words are slurred or strange. T is for Time: call 911 right away.
Write down the time the signs started. Doctors need to know this, because some treatments only work if they are given within a few hours.
Do not give the person anything to eat or drink, because their swallowing may not be safe. Stay with them and keep them calm until help arrives.
zh: 中風是血液到不了部分大腦，或腦裡的血管破裂，腦細胞幾分鐘內就開始死亡，所以快速治療非常重要。BE FAST 幫你記警訊：B 平衡——突然頭暈或走路困難；E 眼睛——一眼或兩眼突然看不清；F 臉——笑的時候一邊臉垂下；A 手臂——兩手舉起時一隻往下掉；S 說話——口齒不清或說話怪；T 時間——馬上打 911。把症狀開始的時間記下來，因為有些治療要在幾小時內給才有效。不要給他吃喝，因為吞嚥可能不安全；陪著他、讓他保持冷靜直到救援到達。

qs.q: What does the F in BE FAST stand for?
qs.why: F is for Face：一邊臉垂下。
qs.evidence: F is for Face

qs.q: Why should you write down the time the signs started?
options: The hospital needs it for the bill
Some treatments only work within a few hours
qs.why: 有些治療要在幾小時內給才有效。
qs.evidence: some treatments only work if they are given within a few hours

qs.q: You should give the person water while you wait for help.
qs.why: 文章說不要給吃喝，吞嚥可能不安全。
qs.evidence: Do not give the person anything to eat or drink

qs.q: "words are slurred" — "slurred" means…
options: not clear and hard to understand
qs.why: slurred 是口齒不清。
qs.evidence: words are slurred or strange

title: Hands-Only CPR for Adults
paras: If an adult suddenly collapses and is not breathing normally, their heart may have stopped. Every minute without help makes survival less likely, so anyone nearby can make a difference.

First, make sure the area is safe. Tap the person and shout, "Are you OK?" If there is no response, call 911, or ask someone else to call and to bring an AED if there is one nearby. An AED is a small machine that can shock the heart back into a normal rhythm.

Next, start chest compressions. Put the heel of one hand in the center of the chest, put your other hand on top, and push hard and fast, at least two inches deep, about 100 to 120 times a minute. Let the chest come back up after each push.
Keep going until the AED arrives, the person starts to breathe normally, or trained help takes over. When the AED arrives, turn it on and follow its voice instructions.
zh: 成年人突然倒下且沒有正常呼吸，心臟可能已經停了。沒有急救的每一分鐘都讓存活機會變低，所以旁邊任何人都能救命。先確認環境安全，拍拍他大聲問「你還好嗎？」沒反應就打 911，或請別人打並拿附近的 AED；AED 是能電擊讓心臟恢復正常節律的小機器。接著胸部按壓：一手掌根放胸部中央，另一手疊上，用力快速按，至少 2 吋（約 5 公分）深、每分鐘約 100 到 120 下，每下讓胸部回彈。一直做到 AED 來、他恢復正常呼吸或專業人員接手；AED 來了就打開，照語音指示做。

qs.q: What should you do first?
options: Make sure the area is safe
qs.why: 第一步：確認環境安全。
qs.evidence: First, make sure the area is safe.

qs.q: How fast should you push?
qs.why: 每分鐘約 100 到 120 下。
qs.evidence: about 100 to 120 times a minute

qs.q: "collapses" in the first paragraph means…
qs.why: collapse 是突然倒下。
qs.evidence: If an adult suddenly collapses

qs.q: An AED gives voice instructions.
qs.why: AED 打開後照它的語音指示做。
qs.evidence: turn it on and follow its voice instructions

title: Eating Well During Chemotherapy
paras: Chemotherapy can change the way food tastes and smells. Many patients feel sick to their stomach, lose their appetite, or get mouth sores. Eating well is still important, because good nutrition helps your body repair itself and fight infection.

Eat small meals five or six times a day instead of three large ones. Choose soft, plain foods, such as rice porridge, eggs, bananas, and crackers. Cold foods often have less smell, so they may be easier to eat.
Drink plenty of fluids between meals, not with them, so you do not feel too full. If you have mouth sores, avoid spicy, salty, or sour food, and use a soft toothbrush.

Take your anti-nausea medicine as the doctor ordered, not only when you already feel sick. Talk to your nurse or a dietitian if you are losing weight. They can suggest high-protein drinks and other ideas.
zh: 化療會改變食物的味道和氣味，很多病人會噁心、沒胃口或口腔破洞，但吃得好還是很重要，營養幫身體修復和對抗感染。一天吃五六次小餐，不要三大餐；選軟、清淡的食物，像稀飯、蛋、香蕉和餅乾；冷的食物味道比較淡，可能比較吃得下。兩餐之間多喝水，不要邊吃邊喝，才不會太飽。口腔破洞時避免辣、鹹、酸，用軟毛牙刷。止吐藥照醫師的時間吃，不要等已經想吐才吃。體重下降就跟護理師或營養師說，他們可以建議高蛋白飲品和其他方法。

qs.q: Why might cold foods be easier to eat?
qs.why: 冷的食物味道比較淡。
qs.evidence: Cold foods often have less smell

qs.q: When should patients drink fluids?
qs.why: 兩餐之間喝，不要邊吃邊喝。
qs.evidence: Drink plenty of fluids between meals, not with them

qs.q: Patients should take anti-nausea medicine only when they already feel sick.
qs.why: 文章說要照醫師的時間吃，不要等想吐才吃。
qs.evidence: not only when you already feel sick

qs.q: "lose their appetite" means…
qs.why: appetite 是胃口；lose their appetite 就是沒胃口。
qs.evidence: lose their appetite

title: Bedside Handoff
paras: At the end of every shift, nurses give a handoff report to the next nurse. In many hospitals, this happens at the patient's bedside instead of at the nurses' station.

Bedside handoff has several benefits. Both nurses can see the patient together, check the IV lines and the wound, and make sure the room is safe. The patient can also join the conversation, correct mistakes, and ask questions.

However, nurses must protect privacy. If there are visitors in the room, the nurse should ask the patient before talking about personal information. Sensitive information can be shared away from the bedside.
A good handoff is short and organized. Many nurses use a structure such as SBAR, and they finish by asking, "Do you have any questions?" A clear handoff helps prevent mistakes during the next shift.
zh: 每班結束時護理師要交班給下一班，很多醫院在病床邊交，而不是在護理站。床邊交班有幾個好處：兩位護理師可以一起看病人、檢查點滴和傷口、確認環境安全；病人也能加入對話、更正錯誤、提出問題。不過要保護隱私：房裡有訪客時，談個人資訊前先問病人；敏感資訊可以離開床邊再交。好的交班簡短有條理，很多護理師用 SBAR 這類架構，最後問一句「你有沒有問題？」清楚的交班能預防下一班出錯。

qs.q: What is the text mainly about?
options: Handoff reports given at the patient's bedside
How to clean a patient's room
qs.why: 整篇在講床邊交班的好處和要注意的地方。

qs.q: Why can the patient's participation help?
options: The patient can write the report
qs.why: 病人可以加入對話、更正錯誤、提問。
qs.evidence: The patient can also join the conversation, correct mistakes, and ask questions.

qs.q: What should the nurse do if there are visitors in the room?
options: Ask the patient before talking about personal information
qs.why: 談個人資訊前先問病人。
qs.evidence: the nurse should ask the patient before talking about personal information

qs.q: Bedside handoff takes longer than handoff at the nurses' station.
qs.why: 文章沒有比較兩種交班花的時間。

title: Getting Ready for a Nursing Job Interview
paras: Many hospitals in the United States interview nurses by video before they make a job offer. For international nurses, the interview is also a test of how clearly they can communicate in English.

Interviewers often ask behavioral questions, such as "Tell me about a time you made a mistake" or "Tell me about a difficult patient." A useful way to answer is the STAR method: describe the Situation, the Task, the Action you took, and the Result.

Prepare three or four real stories from your clinical experience before the interview. Practice telling each story in about two minutes. Focus on what you did and what you learned, not only on what happened.

At the end, you will usually have a chance to ask questions. Good questions show interest, for example, "How long is the orientation for new nurses?" or "What support do you offer international nurses?" Finally, send a short thank-you email the same day.
zh: 很多美國醫院在發聘書前會用視訊面試護理師；對國際護理師來說，面試也在測英文溝通是否清楚。面試官常問行為題，例如「說一次你犯錯的經驗」或「說一位很難照顧的病人」，好用的回答方法是 STAR：情境、任務、你採取的行動和結果。面試前準備三四個真實的臨床故事，每個練到約兩分鐘，重點放在你做了什麼、學到什麼，不只是發生了什麼。最後通常可以發問，好問題能展現興趣，例如新人訓練多久、對國際護理師有什麼支持。當天寄一封簡短的感謝信。

qs.q: What does the A in STAR stand for?
qs.why: A 是你採取的行動（Action）。
qs.evidence: the Action you took

qs.q: How long should each story take?
qs.why: 每個故事練到約兩分鐘說完。
qs.evidence: Practice telling each story in about two minutes.

qs.q: You should send a thank-you email on the same day.
qs.why: 最後一句：當天寄簡短的感謝信。
qs.evidence: send a short thank-you email the same day

qs.q: What is the writer's main advice?
options: Only international nurses need to prepare
Prepare real stories and practice them before the interview
Never ask questions in an interview
qs.why: 全文重點是事先準備真實故事、練習、最後發問與感謝。

title: Your Rights as a Patient
paras: As a patient, you have rights. Knowing them can help you take part in your own care.

You have the right to clear information about your illness, your treatment, and the possible risks and benefits. Before most procedures, a doctor will explain them and ask you to sign a consent form. You may ask questions and take time to decide.

You have the right to privacy. Staff should not share your health information with other people without your permission, except when the law allows it. You also have the right to refuse a treatment, even if your doctor recommends it, after you understand what may happen.

If English is not your first language, you can ask for a medical interpreter. In most US hospitals, this service is free. Family members, especially children, should not be used as interpreters for important medical conversations.
zh: 身為病人你有權利，了解它們能幫你參與自己的照顧。你有權得到清楚的資訊：病情、治療和可能的風險與好處；多數處置前醫師會說明並請你簽同意書，你可以發問、慢慢決定。你有隱私權：除非法律允許，工作人員未經你同意不能把健康資訊告訴別人。你也有權拒絕治療，即使醫師建議，只要你了解可能的後果。英文不是母語的話，可以要求醫療口譯員，大多數美國醫院免費提供；重要的醫療對話不應該請家人，尤其是小孩來翻譯。

qs.q: What can patients do before they sign a consent form?
options: Ask questions and take time to decide
qs.why: 簽之前可以發問、慢慢決定。
qs.evidence: You may ask questions and take time to decide.

qs.q: Patients can refuse a treatment that their doctor recommends.
qs.why: 即使醫師建議，病人了解後果後也有權拒絕。
qs.evidence: You also have the right to refuse a treatment, even if your doctor recommends it

qs.q: Who should NOT be used as interpreters for important conversations?
qs.why: 重要醫療對話不應該請家人，特別是小孩翻譯。
qs.evidence: Family members, especially children, should not be used as interpreters

title: What Is the NCLEX?
paras: Every nurse who wants to work as a registered nurse in the United States must pass the NCLEX-RN, a national licensing exam. Graduates of nursing programs outside the United States take the same exam as American graduates, in English, and it can be taken at test centers in several other countries.

Unlike many school exams, the NCLEX is a computerized adaptive test. This means the computer chooses each new question based on how you answered the questions before it. If you answer correctly, the next question is usually more difficult. Because of this, the number of questions is not the same for everyone, and many test takers feel the exam is hard even when they are doing well.

The exam does not mainly test whether you can remember facts. Instead, it focuses on safe, effective care and clinical judgment. Many questions ask what the nurse should do first, which patient to see first, or which finding needs to be reported to the provider. Newer case-study questions follow one patient through several steps, from recognizing important cues to evaluating the results of care.

For international nurses, reading speed matters. A question about priorities may be only a few sentences long, but a case study can include a nurse's notes, vital signs, and lab results. Practicing nursing questions in English, and not only general English, is one of the best ways to prepare.
zh: 想在美國當註冊護理師都要通過 NCLEX-RN 國家執照考試。美國以外護理系的畢業生考同一份英文考試，也可以在其他幾個國家的考場考。和很多學校考試不同，NCLEX 是電腦適性測驗：電腦依你前面的答題選下一題，答對通常下一題更難，所以每個人題數不同，很多人考得不錯還是覺得很難。考試主要不是考記不記得事實，而是安全有效的照護和臨床判斷：很多題問護理師應該先做什麼、先看哪位病人、哪個發現要通報醫療人員；較新的個案題會跟著一位病人走好幾步，從辨識重要線索到評值照護結果。對國際護理師來說閱讀速度很重要：優先順序題可能只有幾句，但個案題可能有護理紀錄、生命徵象和檢驗值。用英文練護理題，不只練一般英文，是最好的準備方法之一。

qs.q: What is the main purpose of the text?
options: To compare nursing salaries in different countries
To explain what the NCLEX is and how it tests nurses
To teach the history of nursing
qs.why: 全文說明 NCLEX 是什麼、怎麼出題、怎麼準備。

qs.q: What usually happens after you answer a question correctly?
options: The next question is usually more difficult
qs.why: 答對通常下一題更難。
qs.evidence: If you answer correctly, the next question is usually more difficult.

qs.q: Everyone who takes the NCLEX answers the same number of questions.
qs.why: 文章說每個人題數不同。
qs.evidence: the number of questions is not the same for everyone

qs.q: According to the last paragraph, what is one of the best ways to prepare?
qs.why: 用英文練護理題是最好的準備方法之一。
qs.evidence: Practicing nursing questions in English, and not only general English, is one of the best ways to prepare.

qs.q: In paragraph 3, "cues" are…
options: important pieces of information about the patient
qs.why: cue 是線索，這裡指病人身上需要注意的重要資訊。
qs.evidence: from recognizing important cues to evaluating the results of care
